people.peter.role: Apostle of Jesus Christ and fellow elder
people.peter.relations: He writes to believers in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. He sends the letter through Silvanus.
people.peter.meaning: Peter greets believers living as foreigners in the Dispersion. He tells the elders to shepherd the flock willingly. They must not lord it over those in their care. He calls himself a witness of the sufferings of Christ. He sends greetings from Babylon and from Mark, his son.
people.jesus.role: Christ who suffered, rose, and is at God’s right hand
people.jesus.relations: Peter calls him the chief cornerstone and the chief Shepherd. He is also the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
people.jesus.meaning: Peter says God raised Jesus Christ from the dead. Christ suffered for us and left an example. When he was cursed, he did not curse back. He trusted the one who judges righteously. Peter says believers will receive a crown when the chief Shepherd is revealed.
people.sarah.role: Holy woman who called Abraham lord
people.sarah.relations: Peter names her obeying her husband Abraham. He calls his readers her children if they do well.
people.sarah.meaning: Peter tells wives to be gentle and quiet. He says holy women of the past did so. He says Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. Wives are her children if they do well. They must not be put in fear by any terror.
people.abraham.relations: Peter says Sarah obeyed him and called him lord.
people.abraham.meaning: Peter names Abraham only as the one Sarah obeyed. He tells no story about him. The next verse tells husbands to honor their wives as joint heirs.
people.noah.role: Man in whose days the ship was built
people.noah.relations: Peter names his days, when God waited patiently. Eight souls were saved through water.
people.noah.meaning: Peter says some spirits in prison were disobedient in the days of Noah. God waited patiently while the ship was built. Eight souls were saved through water. Peter calls this a symbol of baptism.
people.silas.role: Faithful brother who helped write the letter
people.silas.relations: Peter calls him our faithful brother, as he considers him.
people.silas.meaning: Peter says he wrote this brief letter through Silvanus. The letter says nothing more about what Silvanus did. Peter says the letter shows the true grace of God.
sources.web.summary: The full text of First Peter is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: Peter is the named speaker. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, manuscripts, and the audience’s situation were not checked independently. The identity of the imprisoned spirits was not checked either. Whether Babylon means a real city was not checked. The text assigns no location to the spirits or to Babylon.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-48.summary: The lesson links trials, belonging to God, and teaching to the dead.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-48.limits: For First Peter, the lesson covers chapters 1 through 4. Its account of the spirit world is Church teaching. The Christofferson excerpt in the lesson was read. The full linked talk, Restoration texts, and Greek meanings were not reviewed independently.
sources.brown-peter.summary: Brown says Peter speaks directly to bound workers. She reads this as giving vulnerable hearers a real role.
sources.brown-peter.limits: This is Brown’s own reading. Wider history of household rules and her Greek analysis were not checked independently. The audience’s situation and the books she cites were not checked either. The letter’s instructions keep unequal power. They do not say outright that the relationship should end.
